title: Firmware accepts the tail of an oversized command
impact: A 32-character noise prefix followed by L:100 R:100 on the same line applies full thrust and refreshes the watchdog. Overflow resets the buffer immediately instead of discarding everything until newline. sscanf also accepts trailing garbage.
recommendation: Use a discard-until-newline state, require complete bounded parsing, and add tests for fragmented, oversized and malformed commands. The host C++ probe reproduced both cases without hardware.

title: Heading remains usable after the gyro stops
impact: After one reference and one gyro sample, evaluate(30) reports DEAD_RECKONING and source GYRO with no further gyro data. The ROS adapter keeps publishing at 20 Hz, so consumer message freshness cannot detect the frozen underlying measurement.
recommendation: Track accepted gyro acquisition freshness independently of reference freshness. Expire the relevant estimate, expose degraded GPS-course-only operation separately, and test disconnected IMU with the estimator still running.

title: GPS backlog is restamped as current data
impact: Only one NMEA line is consumed every 0.2 seconds, including ignored sentences. In a fake 10-line/s stream, after ten seconds 50 lines remain queued and the published sample is 4.9 seconds old, yet stamped with the current clock. Actual backlog depends on receiver configuration.
recommendation: Use bounded nonblocking draining, retain the latest complete valid fix, preserve acquisition timing and report serial lag. Reject malformed numeric fields and configure receiver output deliberately.

title: Manual-only bench launch cannot acquire control
impact: The launch starts the stricter arbiter but no safety_monitor. The arbiter now requires a fresh safety stream before MANUAL. This is a compatibility regression introduced by the recent hardening.
recommendation: Provide an explicit supervised bench profile with appropriate site-independent policy and test its complete launch. Do not globally disable supervision to make the bench work.

title: Motor-link recovery can restore thrust without explicit rearm
impact: Serial reconnection is automatic; incoming commands continue to be accepted while disconnected. When the port returns, the next command is sent. STATUS watchdog/applied-output reports are ignored, so the arbiter/UI cannot distinguish requested control from motor-link health.
recommendation: Publish motor-controller health and applied output, latch Hold on loss/reset, and require explicit rearm after a reconnect. Test actual USB disconnect, Arduino reboot and stale queued commands.

title: IMU covariance marks real measurements as absent
impact: Gyro and acceleration are populated, but covariance[0] is -1 in both IMU publishers. ROS Imu defines -1 as no estimate; unknown covariance is all zeros. A compliant future EKF can discard these data. Current custom heading logic ignores the covariance, hiding the mismatch.
recommendation: Publish measured covariance, or unknown zeros pending calibration; reserve -1 for unavailable components. Add an EKF-facing message contract test. See the linked official Imu definition.

title: Sensor frames are incomplete and camera axes disagree
impact: No imu_frame or lidar_frame exists. camera_frame has body-aligned axes, while dock_marker_node reports optical coordinates under the image frame name. Neither runtime launch starts robot_state_publisher. The mesh also points to an old laptop absolute path.
recommendation: Use a portable description with measured sensor mounts, camera optical frame, IMU and LiDAR frames; publish static transforms in hardware and simulation. Add dynamic map/odom transforms only from an actual localization source.

title: Battery display assumes four cells on the documented three-cell boat
impact: The production function classifies 12.6 V as BELOW_RESERVE with zero reserve. Passing cells=3 classifies the same input as OK. This is a display/model error, not a verified battery protection system.
recommendation: Make chemistry/cell count site or hardware configuration; label voltage-derived reserve as an estimate and test configured thresholds. Confirm the installed pack before changing deployment settings.

title: Current sensing depends on unverified hard-coded shunts
impact: Addresses and shunt resistance are fixed in code and documented as unverified. Current is divided by that value, so a mismatch directly scales every current/power reading. There is no sensor-identity or saturation check.
recommendation: Parameterize each channel, verify markings and address, compare readings with known measurements, and mark uncalibrated data explicitly. Do not use it for automatic protection until validated.

title: Post-processing cannot locate normal recorder output
impact: Recorder writes run/bag/rosbag2/*.mcap; finder only glob-searches run/bag/*.mcap. A run path fails discovery. Direct nested-file invocation also selects the wrong run root for manifest merging, and only the first bag file is processed.
recommendation: Resolve the archive root from manifest/metadata, discover all segments deterministically and test using an archive produced by the recorder.

title: Real NavSatFix messages break synchronization processing
impact: build_sync_index reads gps_msg.status as though it were an integer; it is a nested NavSatStatus message. Comparing it with zero raises TypeError.
recommendation: Read status.status and test real ROS-shaped decoded records, including missing and no-fix samples. Synthetic flattened test data must not define the production schema.

title: Missing streams can produce a passing quality report
impact: With camera frames but no GPS or IMU, poor_sync is false and the quality report passes. An empty report also defaults to pass. Drop and sync issues mostly append warnings without failing the result.
recommendation: Define required streams per collection profile, distinguish missing/unknown/degraded/fail, require minimum valid coverage, and make the quality criteria explicit.

title: Sorting removes evidence of out-of-order samples
impact: The loader sorts by log time before validating ordering. The out-of-order check therefore sees sorted input and reports zero. Synchronization also uses arrival/log time rather than sensor acquisition time.
recommendation: Validate original sequence and header timestamps before sorting a separate index; keep both acquisition and receipt clocks, with offset and clock-reset diagnostics.

title: Post-processing invalidates the capture checksum manifest
impact: Capture hashes manifest.json, then post-processing overwrites it without regenerating or separating checksums. All decoded messages, including image payloads, are retained in RAM, which scales poorly with long recordings and LiDAR.
recommendation: Keep immutable capture provenance/checksums and versioned derived reports. Stream metadata/timestamps rather than retaining every decoded sensor payload.

title: Recording storage estimates are too optimistic and no reserve stop exists
impact: 640x480 bgr8 at 10 Hz is 9.216 MB/s or 33.18 GB/hour before overhead, versus the 7 GB/hour planning text. The start threshold is checked only at start; runtime status reports free space but does not stop before exhaustion. LiDAR adds model-dependent traffic.
recommendation: Use observed rate for estimates and a configurable runtime reserve with graceful finalization. Measure actual MCAP storage and include LiDAR profile limits; do not treat the raw calculation as a measured disk rate.

title: Video encoding is unbounded per client
impact: An unchanged cached frame was JPEG-encoded ten times for ten reads with no pacing. Each connected viewer runs another encoder loop; an old frame continues to look like a streaming feed after capture stops.
recommendation: Encode once per new frame, share bytes across clients, bound output FPS/quality and display frame age. Apply the same rule to detection video and future LiDAR previews.

title: Most subsystem status can remain green after its publisher dies
impact: Operator and mission status have arrival times, but cached camera/power/system/recording/dock-marker state has no general expiry. Recording may keep displaying the last true value after the recorder node disappears; a last detected marker can persist after video loss.
recommendation: Give every status source its own timestamp, timeout and unavailable state. Display sensor age separately from transport connectivity. Extend this contract to LiDAR.

title: Non-control buttons still report success without delivery
impact: Recording and detector endpoints return status ok even when ros_node is absent; they do not require matching subsystem acceptance. Several JSON handlers still assume an object. The corrected operator protocol has not been generalized to these commands.
recommendation: Validate input types and use accepted/pending/failed receipts for subsystem actions. Include recorder absent, full disk, model-load failure and no ROS tests.

title: Hold and powered safety stops ramp down in simulation
impact: An ordinary zero target ramps from 30 N in roughly one second. Only the separate e-stop and watchdog paths bypass the ramp. The real driver writes zero immediately, so simulated Hold behavior differs from the control contract and real path.
recommendation: Represent stop intent explicitly or bypass down-ramping for propulsion stops; preserve an intentional acceleration ramp. Test force output, not only arbiter percentages.

title: Simulation time is not wired through the runtime
impact: The bridge has no /clock mapping and the launch does not set use_sim_time. Heading/GPS velocity math uses callback wall-time intervals although Gazebo sensors follow simulation timing. Slow or accelerated simulation changes estimated speed and course gating.
recommendation: Use simulation time for sensor/physics calculations and retain monotonic/steady clocks for operator watchdogs. Test pause and changed real-time factor deliberately.

title: Simulation cleanup can kill unrelated processes and leave duplicates
impact: The script globally SIGKILLs generic names including web_server and safety_monitor, but omits control_arbiter and heading_estimator. It can affect another stack and still leave duplicate controller/heading publishers.
recommendation: Manage a launch process group/PID set, shut down gracefully, and verify exactly one expected node per domain. Separate simulation and hardware ROS domains.

title: Network access is also control authority
impact: The server binds all interfaces with no authentication; Foxglove also exposes a separate ROS bridge. Operator session IDs provide ordering, not identity/security. The phone-hotspot/boat-modem network and reachable interfaces are not configured in this repository.
recommendation: Define the trusted network boundary, authenticate command access, restrict bridge capabilities and use an encrypted private path when crossing networks. Test routing/reconnect separately from internet access; do not expose raw command ports publicly.

title: Heading and calibration are not ready for global LiDAR fusion
impact: COG is travel direction, not bow yaw. A fixed 0.3 m displacement gate rejects clean 1 m/s motion at 5 Hz (0.2 m per fix); GPS noise can dominate consecutive-fix direction. The filter also accepts invalid speed by retaining an older valid speed.
recommendation: Separate course, body attitude and map pose. Accumulate displacement over a suitable window, use receiver velocity/quality where available, reject invalid inputs, and calibrate before choosing an EKF. Start LiDAR visualization in the boat frame.

title: Launch and documentation no longer describe one consistent system
impact: The gaps page still says stale safety returns to nominal and command IDs do not exist; the current code differs. The simulation package launches boat_perception without declaring it as a runtime dependency. Recorder remains opt-in, and runtime launch does not include TF.
recommendation: Update a single capability matrix with implemented/offline-tested/sim-tested/hardware-tested states. Add all launched package dependencies and launch smoke tests; keep hardware, bench and simulation profiles explicit.
